title: Periodic Relocation of Popular Schools to Better Align School Access with Principles of Meritocracy and Social Mixing
what_it_is: Periodic Relocation of Popular Schools to Better Align School Access with Principles of Meritocracy and Social Mixing

sections.label: Relocating popular schools, admissions review
sections.summary: MOE considers relocating schools, including popular ones, to areas with higher demand and will review admissions policies for accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider periodically relocating popular schools to neighbourhoods with different housing and socioeconomic status (SES) mixes to better align school access with the principles of meritocracy and social mixing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We take into account several factors, including current and projected school-going populations in each residential area, as well as the supply of places provided by the schools in the vicinity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: When the demand for school places falls or is projected to fall in a particular area, we will consider relocating schools in that area, including popular schools, to areas with higher demand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: MOE will continue to review our school admissions policies so that our schools continue to remain accessible to children from all backgrounds.

sections.label: Admin data, housing types, social mixing
sections.summary: The Member asks whether MOE would use primary intake admin data by housing type and prioritise social mixing for schools with little public housing nearby.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would MOE consider tapping on the admin data of primary school intake profile by housing types, as well as identify schools, within two-kilometre radius, have little, or very low, or no public housing, and prioritise social mixing measures for such schools?

sections.label: MOE-OBS Challenge student mixing
sections.summary: The MOE-OBS Challenge brings Secondary 3 students from different schools together outdoors to mix, make friends and overcome challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member spoke about the, I believe, the MOE-OBS Challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, Secondary 3 students across different schools, living together, coming together over a period of time to explore the outdoors, out of their comfort zone, a great opportunity for them to mix, to mingle, to make friends and to build connections, but also for them to overcome challenges together.

sections.label: Combined school co-curricular activities
sections.summary: Combined school CCAs let three schools that cannot each form a team come together to form a team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For instance, we have a combined school co-curricular activities (CCAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It solves a practical challenge, so we have these three schools, on their own, not able to form a team, but coming together, they form a formidable team.

sections.label: RI boarding programme mixing students
sections.summary: RI's boarding programme lets RI students and students from several named secondary schools spend time together mixing and learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, Raffles Institution (RI) has a RI boarding programme and I have a list here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is an opportunity for RI students, together with students from Guangyang Secondary School, Pierce Secondary, Whitley Secondary School, Deyi Secondary School, Kuo Chuan Presbyterian Secondary School, Sengkang Secondary School, Bowen Secondary School, and a few others – students will come together, spend a period of time together, mixing, mingling, learning from one another, doing things together.

sections.label: Distance, proximity, Phase 2C places
sections.summary: Distance matters for primary schools, so Phase 2C ring-fences places for children based on proximity, regardless of school links.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There is also the element of distance, because when it comes to schools, particularly primary schools, we would like to also support proximity, convenience, easy for the children to go to school and come back home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, that is where Phase 2C comes in, where a certain number of places is ring-fenced for children, regardless of whether they have any links or affiliation to the school or not, premise on the basis of proximity.
